title: Board fullscreen falls back to filling the window

v:
# Board fullscreen falls back to filling the window

## Context

siren-board's control bar had no way to make the board bigger than the container the page gave
it, so a reader presenting a diagram or studying a large one could only pan and zoom inside that
box. The Fullscreen API covers desktop browsers, but not every place a board is shown: iPhone
Safari does not take an ordinary element fullscreen, and an iframe without `allowfullscreen`
refuses the request. A button that does nothing in those places, or that is hidden there, leaves
exactly the readers on small screens without it. Safari's prefixed
`webkitRequestFullscreen` would reach some of them, at the cost of a second code path to keep
correct.

## Decision

1. **Fullscreen** is the state in which the board fills the whole screen. Where the Fullscreen
   API can be used, it is the screen's fullscreen: the board's container becomes
   `document.fullscreenElement`. Where it cannot — the container has no `requestFullscreen`,
   `document.fullscreenEnabled` is not `true`, or the request is rejected — the board fills the
   browser window instead (**fill**). Both are `board.fullscreen === true`; a caller cannot tell
   them apart, and no option, member or callback says which one is in use.
2. Fullscreen is independent of the **View**, the **Step**, **Playback** and the **Full
   diagram**: switching it changes none of them and does not re-render.
3. Prefixed APIs (`webkitRequestFullscreen`, `webkitExitFullscreen`) are not used; an
   environment that only has them gets fill.

## Consequences

- `board.fullscreen`, `board.setFullscreen(on)` and `BoardOptions.onFullscreenChange` follow the
  shape of `fullDiagram` / `setFullDiagram` / `onFullDiagramChange`, and the built-in bar gains a
  Fullscreen button after Reset view that works everywhere.
- In fill, Escape leaves it, as it leaves the screen's fullscreen; an Escape something else has
  already handled (`defaultPrevented`, or a dropdown that stops it) does not.
- Fill does not lock page scrolling or manage other `position: fixed` elements on the page; the
  board sits above them at the highest z-index.
- Both the screen's fullscreen and fill draw the board on `--siren-board-surface`, so the browser's
  default black backdrop never shows.
- Because the mode is not exposed, a later change to how fill or the screen's fullscreen is
  achieved (a prefixed API, a different fill technique) is not a breaking change.
